item.title: Wiz Khalifa’s Romanian Prison Judgment Annulled As Appeal Returns
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiz Khalifa's nine-month Romanian prison judgment was annulled, but prosecutors' appeal returns to court November 12.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa no longer faces an active nine-month Romanian prison judgment after a Bucharest court annulled the ruling and canceled its enforcement warrant.

The November 3 decision changes his position, but it does not end the criminal case.

The Bucharest Court of Appeal set a new hearing for November 12 at 4 p.m. local time. Judges will rehear an appeal filed by prosecutors from Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism, known as DIICOT.

The court told Wiz’s chosen lawyer about the date and ordered steps to arrange the rapper’s appearance by videoconference.

The court’s short order, translated from Romanian, says it “cancels the prison sentence enforcement warrant.” The judges also struck down the December 18, 2025 decision that imposed the nine-month term.

The case began at the “Beach, Please!” festival in Costinesti on July 13, 2024. Prosecutors said Wiz had 18.53 grams of cannabis and a cannabis cigarette for personal use.

He smoked onstage during his performance and was later charged with illegal possession of a risk drug.

A trial court first imposed a criminal fine of 3,600 lei. DIICOT appealed, and the Constanta Court of Appeal replaced that fine with nine months in prison in December 2025.

An enforcement warrant followed. By May, Romanian authorities had placed Wiz on a wanted list, raising the prospect of detention during European travel.

The new hearing will not restart the whole case. It returns to the appeal that DIICOT filed against the 3,600-lei fine.

That appeal produced the prison term and warrant that Bucharest judges have now erased, so the result of the rehearing will decide the next turn in the case.

His lawyers kept challenging the result. Romania’s highest court moved the dispute from Constanta to Bucharest in September.

On October 20, AllHipHop reported that the Bucharest court had allowed one part of his annulment challenge to move forward.

At that stage, the prison judgment still stood.

The November 3 ruling goes further by removing that judgment and its enforcement warrant. It does not amount to an acquittal, and prosecutors have not dropped their appeal.

The court will hear DIICOT’s challenge to the original fine again on November 12, with Wiz expected to join the proceeding remotely if the videoconference arrangements are completed.

item.title: Takeoff Murder Trial Rescheduled For April 2027
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Patrick Xavier Clark's trial in Takeoff's killing is now set for April 2027, months after its planned November 2026 start.
item.content:encoded:
Patrick Xavier Clark’s murder trial in the killing of Takeoff is now set for April 15, 2027, moving the case out of its planned November start.

The Harris County District Clerk’s public docket lists a 9 A.M. trial setting on April 15 for Clark’s murder case. The setting is marked as a jury trial. The same docket shows that an October 8 pretrial conference was “Reset Upon Defense Request.”

The public record does not say when the April date was first entered. It was visible when the docket was reviewed on November 3. Cause No. 179722001010 remains active, and Clark is listed as free on bond.

That is a major shift from the schedule announced earlier this year. Clark’s attorney at the time told KPRC 2 in February that the trial would begin November 9, with jury selection starting November 5.

Clark is charged with murder in the November 1, 2022 shooting that killed Takeoff, whose legal name was Kirsnick Khari Ball. Prosecutors have accused Clark of firing toward a group outside 810 Billiards & Bowling in downtown Houston after an argument connected to a dice game. Takeoff was not involved in the game or the dispute, police said.

Investigators have said surveillance video showed Clark pointing and firing a gun. They also said his fingerprints were found on a wine bottle left at the scene. Clark has consistently denied firing the fatal shots, and his defense team maintains that he did not kill the 28-year-old Migos rapper.

The defense has continued working on the physical evidence as the case moved toward trial. In September, Clark asked for access to the bullets and other evidence held by Houston police so an independent expert could examine the material.

Clark also changed lawyers in March. Court filings showed that Houston defense attorney Kent Schaffer replaced Letitia Quinones-Hollins, while Dan Cogdell and Anthony Osso joined the team. The current docket lists Schaffer as Clark’s attorney of record.

The April setting comes more than four years after Takeoff was killed. Two other people were wounded in the shooting and survived. Clark was arrested in December 2022, released on $1 million bond in January 2023 and indicted on a murder charge that May. His next listed setting is the April jury trial.

item.title: Smoke DZA Pairs “We Outside” With Grassroots Voter Organizing
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Smoke DZA joined Popular Democracy for We Outside, connecting a Bun B and Benny the Butcher-assisted project to voter organizing.
item.content:encoded:
Smoke DZA and Popular Democracy released We Outside on November 2, pairing a rap project with a push for community involvement before the midterms.

Mike & Keys produced the release, which features Bun B, Benny the Butcher, BIG K.R.I.T., Kai Kash and Fergie Baby.

The project is an EP credited to Smoke DZA and Mike & Keys, with six songs running 16 minutes. Its catalog gives the same November 2 release date and an RFC Music Group copyright line.

“Our voices matter, and we have to show up, get involved, and have a say in what happens next,” Smoke DZA said in the project announcement.

Popular Democracy said its affiliates were reaching voters through calls and door knocking while offering election protection training. The network organizes Black, Latine, immigrant and working-class communities.

A clothing collaboration with Union Los Angeles and Barriers adds hoodies, sweatshirts and T-shirts to the project.

The partnership follows another Popular Democracy event that put performers in the same room as organizers. Its July 9 People’s Convention and Let’s Get Free concert took place at the Hyatt Regency Crystal City in Arlington, Virginia.

The event marked the 14th Amendment’s anniversary.

Dead Prez, Mumu Fresh and Flor De Toloache headlined, with Kemba and Roque Starz among the other performers, The Washington Informer reported.

The use of music to reach voters also extends beyond this project. In a separate effort, DJs at the Polls sent about 2,000 DJs to nearly 5,000 polling sites across 24 states on November 3.

Founder Anton Moore developed the idea while working on BET’s “Rap City.” The sets come with training and rules against partisan promotion.

Popular Democracy also named housing, health care and immigration enforcement among the issues it plans to organize around after November 3.

item.title: Kool DJ Red Alert Announces Radio Farewell After Decades Of Breaking Hip-Hop Legends
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kool DJ Red Alert plans a four-hour WBLS sendoff as his KISS-FM roots and work with BDP and Native Tongues mark a lasting legacy.
item.content:encoded:
Kool DJ Red Alert is leaving radio with a four-hour farewell set on WBLS after more than four decades of helping Hip-Hop reach new listeners.

The New York pioneer announced the sendoff on Instagram, calling it his final broadcast on the station that now carries his mixes.

“KOOL DJ RED ALERT FAREWELL TO RADIO!” he wrote in the announcement on his official Instagram account.

For listeners who grew up taping his shows, that farewell closes a run that helped shape which rappers New York heard first.

Before radio, the Harlem DJ drew inspiration from Kool Herc and brought his own turntables into neighborhood parks.

Red began broadcasting on KISS-FM in October 1983, bringing records from the clubs onto a commercial station while Hip-Hop was still building its audience.

His support gave early exposure to Boogie Down Productions and Native Tongues artists, including Jungle Brothers, De La Soul and A Tribe Called Quest.

Queen Latifah and Black Sheep also benefited from his ear for new talent, long before streaming playlists offered artists another path to listeners.

Red’s ties to those acts went beyond choosing records, with his nephew Mike G helping form the Jungle Brothers alongside friends.

NAMM’s oral history also documents Red Alert Productions, his management company that worked with Jungle Brothers, Tribe, Monie Love and Black Sheep.

His KISS-FM platform became part of the Bridge Wars as he championed KRS-One and Scott La Rock against the rival WBLS camp.

Mr. Magic and Marley Marl backed MC Shan, while Red played BDP’s “South Bronx” as the records turned radio competition into rap history.

“We always kept everything on records and everything verbal,” Red told The Village Voice in a 2012 interview about that rivalry.

His own radio path later took him through Hot 97 and back to KISS, with WBLS becoming another home for the veteran DJ.

AllHipHop reported his KISS return in 2001 after he left Hot 97, when he described an outlook that had carried him through change.

“The main thing is, if one door closes, another one opens,” Red said at the time about that move.

His four-hour farewell DJ set is scheduled for Monday, November 30, 2026, on New York’s 107.5 WBLS.

item.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms Makes History In Georgia & Hakeem Jeffries Moves Closer To House Speakership
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Keisha Lance Bottoms secured an unprecedented triumph as the governor of Georgia, a first for an African American woman.
item.content:encoded:
Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia’s governorship Tuesday to become the first Black woman elected governor of a U.S. state.

Election night also brought Brooklyn’s Hakeem Jeffries closer to a historic House speakership.

Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, defeated Republican businessman Rick Jackson, securing a breakthrough that extended beyond Georgia. Bottoms will become the state’s first Black governor and first woman governor in American histoy when she takes office.

Her victory also ended more than two decades of Republican control of the governor’s office.

In Washington, another potential first came into view.

Democrats are projected to regain the House majority, positioning Hakeem Jeffries to become the first Black speaker in the chamber’s history. The Brooklyn congressman would succeed Republican Mike Johnson if he wins the required vote when the new Congress convenes in January.

Voters elect House members, who then choose the speaker.

That means the election results opened Jeffries’ path to the position, but did not formally give him the gavel. The House elects its speaker at the beginning of a new Congress.

Together, the developments placed Black political leadership at the center of an election with consequences for both state government and national power.

Bottoms’ victory followed a career that included service in Atlanta government and the Biden White House. She previously worked as a senior adviser to former President Joe Biden and directed the White House Office of Public Engagement.

She will succeed Republican Gov. Brian Kemp, who is leaving after two consecutive terms. 

Her campaign emphasized affordable health care, housing and education. Among her proposals were eliminating state income taxes for teachers and expanding access to job training, according to WSB-TV. Those priorities will accompany her into an office no Black woman has previously held in any U.S. state. 

Jeffries already holds a place in congressional history as the first Black person to lead a major party in Congress. Becoming speaker would carry that achievement into a position responsible for presiding over the House and helping direct its business.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Makes Surprise New Hampshire Polling Place Stop On Election Day
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nicki Minaj made a surprise Election Day appearance near a Derry, New Hampshire, polling place after campaigning in Michigan.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj made a surprise Election Day appearance near a polling place in Derry, New Hampshire, on Tuesday night, November 3. The visit came one week after she campaigned with Donald Trump in Michigan.

NBC reported the New Hampshire sighting in its election live coverage. The stop put Minaj back in the political news on the final day of voting. It also moved her campaign activity from Michigan to a state with a competitive Senate race.

The Michigan event included support for Trump and Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, according to The Daily Beast.

In Derry, Minaj was seen near a polling site during a Republican push to get voters to the polls.

She was not the only famous face tied to that effort. Rob Gronkowski, Riley Gaines, Floyd Mayweather, Mike Tyson and Danny Amendola were among the other public figures involved.

Their appearances added sports and entertainment names to the final hours of the campaign.

New Hampshire’s competitive Senate contest between Chris Pappas and John Sununu was a major part of the final campaign push. NHPR reported that candidates were closing their campaigns while Turning Point volunteers canvassed in Salem.

That work was separate from the Derry sighting, but it showed the wider race to reach voters before polls closed.

Derry’s official election page listed the general election for November 3. It named Pinkerton Academy as the town’s polling site, with voting from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

The reports about Minaj only placed her near a polling location in Derry. They did not identify Pinkerton Academy as her exact location.

The Senate contest was also among the key New Hampshire races outlined in the Associated Press election notes.

That gave Minaj’s visit a clear political backdrop without turning the sighting into a statement on any one local race.

In a separate same-day development, Rep. Jasmine Crockett criticized Minaj’s political motives during a TMZ interview in New York City. Crockett said Minaj was “only out for herself.”

TMZ reported that Crockett also raised tension between Minaj’s immigrant background and Trump-era ICE detentions, then urged public voices to help bring people together.

Crockett’s comments were not reported as a response to the New Hampshire appearance. The interview and the Derry sighting happened on the same day, but the available reporting did not connect them.

For Minaj, the Derry visit made two political appearances in two states within a week. The first was a campaign stop with Trump and Rogers in Michigan.

The second put her near voters in New Hampshire while the Republican turnout push was underway.

No eligible report supplied remarks from Minaj at the Derry appearance. That leaves the location, timing and link to the wider turnout effort as the main facts from her Election Day stop.

item.title: Jamie Foxx Reveals He Is Planning To Move To Australia
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jamie Foxx, 58, said he planned to find a home in Australia and revealed a family surprise for Alyce Huckstepp at the Melbourne Cup.
item.content:encoded:
Jamie Foxx, 58, said he planned to find a home in Australia while discussing his future with girlfriend Alyce Huckstepp during an appearance at the Melbourne Cup on Tuesday, November 3.

“Of course, I’m moving. I’ma find a place,” Foxx told the Daily Mail in an exclusive interview.

The actor spoke inside the Don Julio Hacienda marquee at Flemington Racecourse, where he also shared a surprise he had arranged for his Australian partner, who is from Queensland. Foxx said he planned to bring her relatives in for the occasion.

“My girl is from Australia, and I’m bringing her whole family here as a surprise,” he said after their relationship had a public break along the way.

Multiple sources told People in January 2025 that Foxx and Huckstepp had separated after dating for about a year and a half. They were first publicly linked in August 2023, when they joined a group at Nobu in Malibu.

Huckstepp had also supported Foxx at work, visiting the set of a BetMGM commercial in July 2024, according to the magazine’s reporting.

They later reunited, and Foxx described her as his girlfriend at Flemington. Their relationship has also prompted questions about expanding their family.

AllHipHop reported on pregnancy claims in May, while noting that neither Foxx, Huckstepp nor their representatives had publicly confirmed the news at that point.

Australia is also where Foxx is working on a film. He is filming the action thriller “Deadlocked” in Victoria for Amazon MGM Studios, giving his time in Melbourne a work connection alongside the personal one.

The production is using Melbourne’s central business district, Docklands and Port Melbourne to recreate New York.

Foxx plays a former Marine who is grieving and serving on a jury when a defendant’s daughter takes control of the courthouse in an attempt to free her father. His character is forced into action during the takeover.

Nikhil Bhat is directing the film, with Sasha Calle, KiKi Layne and Luke Hemsworth joining Foxx in the cast. Foxx is also producing through Foxxhole Productions. His daughter Corinne Foxx is an executive producer, putting another family connection behind his current Australian project.

item.title: Claressa Shields Previews Debut Album With Papoose In Atlanta
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Claressa Shields previewed her debut album before a packed Atlanta crowd, but can Ressa Da GWOAT turn celebrity curiosity into repeat listeners?
item.content:encoded:
Claressa Shields is taking this rap thing seriously and has no intention of letting her debut album arrive quietly. She got down to it recently.

The boxing champion brought out more than 500 guests for an Atlanta listening party for What Did You Expect. Nine tracks got their introduction, and Shields performed several selections herself for the audience. That is a a lot more than freestyles and social media hijinks. Shout out to photographer Freddie O for documenting this for us all. Here come the questions.

Can Claressa build a following that comes for the songs and stays beyond the celebrity curiosity? That is the challenge with any athlete entering Hip-Hop. Getting people to press play once is achievable. Getting them to put you in their regular rotation takes something else.

Performing as Ressa Da GWOAT, Shields certainly has a memorable name. Imagine being the opening act and having to follow that introduction with your modest little stage name.

Papoose attended the festivities, along with Scrappy, Dondria, Hotboy Turk, Jhonni Blaze and others. Pap also joined Shields onstage. His presence is hardly surprising, considering their relationship, but having a respected lyricist in your corner gives rap fans another reason to pay attention.

It also guarantees that somebody will ask what advice he is giving her. I would like to hear that conversation myself.

The event celebrated “Party,” her lead single, which already has a music video. There is still no announced release date for the album, so everybody demanding a verdict might have to exercise a little patience.

“We dropping more heat next week!!!!!!”

That was part of Ressa’s celebratory message following the event. She sounds pleased with how the night went, and understandably so.

My position? Let the woman release her music. Then judge the music. Boxing greatness does not automatically produce a great album, but it should not disqualify somebody from trying either. We have plenty sports people try this.

The title What Did You Expect invites commentary and I cannot wait to see what comes out of it. Claressa knows people are watch…now how many will keep listening.

Here are some of the new songs:

It does not sound like Pap is writing for her, by the way.

item.title: Cardi B Calls Out “Rage Bait” Over Javits Frimpong’s Killing
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B accused a user named Kyle of using edited clips of her bullying comments to turn Javits Frimpong's death into rage bait.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B accused a social media user named Kyle of using the killing of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong as “rage bait,” after clips of her comments about bullying spread online.

In a later Instagram post, the Bronx rapper said parts of her livestream had been edited to encourage attacks on celebrities. She argued that the clips drew attention away from the teenager’s death.

“What happened to Javits is very serious,” Cardi wrote.

She also told Kyle that, as a gay Black man, he should understand how people could be targeted, bullied and left without protection.

The dispute followed her appeal to parents to confront bullying. On Instagram Live, Cardi had urged adults to take responsibility for how their children treated other kids.

“Teach your kids to be fucking kind because it starts with you,” she said.

Cardi had criticized parents who brushed aside teachers’ complaints about their children’s behavior. Buying kids sneakers and giving them attention did not excuse cruelty toward classmates, she argued.

She said harassment could lead young people to seek safety in gangs, linking that point to her own experience “because that’s practically what happened to me.”

She also said U.S.-born children could target newcomers whose families came from the same country. She rejected the idea that one racial or ethnic group alone was responsible for the bullying.

Frimpong was shot while walking to school in the Bronx on October 29. Students at DreamYard Preparatory School walked out Monday, November 2 to honor him and call for action against bullying and gun violence.

“We had to go through the same thing he went through. From elementary to now. We deal with racism, colorism,” student Miriam Tourkire said.

Friends described a boy who made people laugh. Some also said they felt safe inside school, where they believed the principal had worked to address an earlier incident, but feared what could happen outside.

His father and friends said he had been involved in an altercation the week before the shooting and that two students had been suspended.

Police had not established a motive. Chief of Detectives Joseph Kenny said investigators were considering possible bullying, a robbery gone wrong or mistaken identity. Police were seeking three teenage boys and had made no arrests, ABC7 New York reported.

item.title: Pusha T Defends Rap Battles But Draws Line Beyond The Music
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Pusha T weighs in on Jay-Z's concerns about rap feuds, with his own Drake clash and past remarks on fatherhood as context.
item.content:encoded:
Pusha T still sees a place for rap battles, but he wants the fight to stay in the songs. Asked about Jay-Z’s concerns over beef culture, the Clipse rapper defended the contest while saying some disputes have crossed the line.

“This is a very competitive sport,” he told The Wall Street Journal. “As long as it’s music, it’s fine. Anything outside of that realm, it’s overboard.”

Pusha also made clear that he did not know which specific clashes Jay had in mind when discussing the harm from rap feuds.

Jay’s own comments focused on what happens after the songs, including online attacks that turn a musical clash into a much wider conflict.

Speaking to GQ about Kendrick Lamar and Drake, Jay questioned whether battles still help Hip-Hop when listeners become fixed in opposing camps.

“It’s too far. It’s bringing people’s kids in it. I don’t like that,” Jay said.

Pusha’s answer carries its own history, since his 2018 fight with Drake brought the Toronto rapper’s son into one of Hip-Hop’s biggest feuds.

“The Story of Adidon” followed Drake’s “Duppy Freestyle” and Pusha’s “Infrared,” turning a string of musical shots into a dispute over family.

Drake addressed fatherhood on Scorpion the following month, disputing the claim that he had hidden his son rather than tried to guard his privacy.

That distinction put a child’s life at the center of a battle that began with attacks on the rappers’ work and credibility. Pusha later spoke about that part of rap conflict from the other side after he became a father to his own son.

During a 2022 appearance on Desus & Mero, he explained why references to children felt different once he had a family himself.

“I don’t like the energy of mentioning my son in that type of energy or any kid in that type of energy,” he said.

AllHipHop covered that shift as Pusha discussed moving past the Drake dispute, while also making clear that he would protect his child.

Pusha and Jay have also shared records, with Pharrell Williams joining them on “Neck & Wrist” from Pusha’s 2022 album It’s Almost Dry.

Jay also voiced remorse over his own battle: “I actually regret that because I really like Nas.”
